text:
ops-bot: ALERT - High tail latency detected for /v1/generate (p99 2.4s). SLO p99=1.2s. Paging: @eng-sre-oncall. Link: https://monitoring.redwood/g/alerts/1832004567

noah: got it, picking this up — I'm the oncall. starting collection of traces and perf logs.

lee: i'm watching grafana now, seeing a spike in batch latency starting ~02:29 UTC. looks correlated with a burst in qps from a single customer org.

noah: any 5xx rate?

matt: 5xxs are low (~0.02%), mostly latencies. customers still getting responses but elevated tail.

noah: ok. first mitigation: switch routing for that org to the fallback model variant (quantized-1) to reduce kernel time. can someone run the routing override?

ashley: I'll send the org-specific override to routing service. doing now.

ops-bot: ACTION TAKEN - routing override applied for org-6789 -> quantized-1.

lee: after override p99 dropped to ~1.1s for that org, cluster-wide p99 still ~1.8s. seems cross-tenant noisy neighbor + one larger backlog of KV items.

noah: starting a short autoscale bump to Dedicated pool (add 2 nodes, timeout 5m). matt, please watch queue depth on GPUs.

matt: autoscale request submitted. GPUs ramping, queue depth decreasing.

eva: customer-impact note: logged 3 paying customers with >10% latency degradation window 02:28–02:46 UTC. no error retries observed. filing to incident status.

noah: good. bridging to handoff — i'll own mitigation until 03:30 then hand to lee for daytime follow-up. putting a note in the incident channel and assigning tasks.

ashley: on customer comms: will draft a short note explaining transient latency, actions taken (routing override + autoscale), and current status.

lee: once everyone is stable, we should tune the alert rule. current alert fires on 1m p99 >1.2s, which caused noise. propose change: evaluate p99 over 5m window and require sustained qps>50 before paging. also add suppression if triggered by single-org spike (use anomaly detector on qps per org).

sanjay: agree. concrete rule suggestion:
```
- alert: HighTailLatency
  expr: histogram_quantile(0.99, sum(rate(request_duration_seconds_bucket[5m])) by (le)) > 1.8
  for: 5m
  labels: severity:page
  annotations: runbook: https://runbooks.redwood/latency-p99
```
This raises the threshold and requires 5m sustained. we can also add a note to check per-org qps.

noah: +1. Also add a companion alert for per-org spikes (non-paging) so platform can auto-apply routing overrides before paging the team.

lee: for the post-incident retro, I'd like a dedicated Grafana dashboard that we can reuse: "Incident Retrospective - Latency & Root Causes". panels to include: p50/p90/p99 (global + per-org top 5), request rate by org, error % by service, GPU utilization, queue depth, batch size distribution, KV cache hit ratio, model variant routing %, recent rollout events, and top slow traces (sampled).

matt: also add a panel showing active autoscale events + node count over time (helps tie latency dips to scaling).

eva: from customer impact side please add a "customers affected" table (org name, impacted window, percent degradation). that'll help SRE+CS review.

ashley: i can own the dashboard wireframe. planning to include drilldowns: click a per-org point -> pre-filtered logs/traces + recent prompt samples.

sanjay: we should also add golden signals panel, and a single-row status at top (OK/WARN/INCIDENT) that maps to open alerts.

noah: sounds good. let's capture action items:
- lee: create Grafana dashboard skeleton + share link (ETA EOD)
- sanjay: update alert rules (5m window + higher threshold) and add per-org spike detector (ETA tomorrow morning)
- ashley: draft customer communication and incident page (ETA 1h)
- matt: add autoscale + node-history panel (with node tags)
- eva: compile affected-customers table and add to retro (ETA 2h)

lee: I'll spin up dashboard and push a temporary link: https://grafana.redwood/d/incident-retro/1832004567 — this is a work-in-progress. please add comments on panels you want changed.

noah: thanks. quick note on alert noise: let's add a small suppression rule that ignores alerts if triggered by <=2 hosts and overall qps < 30 for that cluster. prevents paging on tiny blips.

sanjay: implementing suppression prototype now, will test against the 02:28 trace and replay.

ashley: posted a short customer note in #customer-updates, cc: @support-leads. kept it vague and reassuring, offered post-incident follow-up.

matt: GPUs back to baseline, latency p99 stable ~1.05s cluster-wide. autoscale nodes removed.

noah: handing off to lee at 03:30 UTC. please continue with dashboard + alert changes, we'll review in the incident retro tomorrow. thanks all. :thumbsup:

lee: taking over. will queue a retro invite and link to dashboard.

ops-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE - status: mitigated, impact: degraded latency for 18 minutes, customers affected: 3, severity: sev3.

noah: filing a short blameless postmortem and tagging this channel. we should keep the retro focused on: alert thresholds, per-org routing mitigations, and dashboard drilldowns.

lee: noted. starting a draft PR for the dashboard panels and adding a checklist for runbook updates.

sanjay: after we confirm changes, i'd like to add an automated test that replays 02:28 traffic shape to staging to validate alerting/overrides.

ashley: added follow-up: coordinate with CS for customer-specific notes if they request details.

noah: great. closing oncall loop. everyone please add any leftover items to the incident board.

lee: closing thread but will post the dashboard PR link once created.
